title: To Nextcloud a signed-off document and a moved document look the same
content:
Nextcloud syncs and shares files, and its activity feed reflects exactly that: a stream of file events. A document being signed off and a document being moved produce entries of the same kind, so the feed cannot distinguish a decision from a filing action.

This is a sharper version of the general document-management gap. The system is not missing a log; it has a detailed one. What it is missing is a type distinction between events that change where a file is and events that change what the organisation has committed to. Powerhouse records the decision the file represents, which is a different object from the file.

Three leads carry this finding — in FR, DE and CH, all at "3 · later". For partners who deploy Nextcloud as a sovereign alternative to hosted file services, the gap is worth naming precisely, because the usual objection is that the activity feed already covers it.

---

## Leads sharing this finding (3)

**3 · later**
- Arawa (FR) — https://arawa.fr
- Compaso GmbH (DE) — https://compaso.de
- Linuxfabrik GmbH (CH Zurich) — https://linuxfabrik.ch

Verbatim research text this claim was extracted from:

> Nextcloud syncs and shares files; its activity feed is a file-event stream, not a business record. A signed-off document and a moved document look the same to it. Powerhouse records the decision the file represents.
description: Its activity feed is a file-event stream rather than a business record, so the decision the file represents has to be recorded somewhere the file's lifecycle cannot reach.
